content:
Fireflies.ai Transcript

Meeting: Meter reconciliation sync - Finance x Product x Telemetry
Date: Feb 12, 2026
Time: 9:00 AM PT
Duration: 38 min
Recorded by: Fireflies.ai

Attendees:
- Talia Benson (Program Manager)
- Laura Bennett (CFO / Finance Exec Sponsor)
- Emily Stone (Billing Controls)
- Rishi Malhotra (FP&A)
- Chris Osei (Product Ops)
- Logan Wright (Telemetry & Analytics)
- Nadia Rahman (Metering Pipelines)
- Allison Grant (Observability)
- Sofia Mendes (Commercial Counsel)
- Chloe Martin (Console Reporting)

---

Summary (auto-generated):
Team reviewed January and February metering reconciliation progress, top defect categories (streaming disconnect accounting, rounding mismatch, retries/double counting, missing dimensions), and publication timeline for internal guidance (meter definitions + dispute runbook + enablement FAQ). Agreed on acceptance thresholds for reconciliation deltas and the sign-off path for any changes that impact invoicing.

Topics:
1) Status: Sample A (Jan) reconciliation and open variances
2) Status: Sample B (Feb) including streaming + retry cases
3) Defects found: rounding, streaming disconnects, retries
4) Auditability: meter_version, invoice_run_id, aggregation windows
5) Guidance publish timeline + Sales/CS enablement
6) Legal language alignment and dispute windows

Questions (auto-generated):
- Do we ever bill tokens after a client disconnect in streaming?
- Are we rounding per-request or at invoice aggregation?
- How do retries show up (and should they be billed)?
- What’s the acceptable variance threshold before we hold an invoice?

Action Items (auto-generated):
- Telemetry team to confirm request outcome / retry dimension semantics and update pipeline
- Finance to confirm tolerance thresholds and notify Support if any customers should be proactively contacted
- Product Ops to annotate experiment readouts with measurement caveats
- Console team to re-run alignment checks after rounding change

---

Transcript:

[00:00] Talia Benson: Alright, cool. I think we’re good to start. This is the cross-functional meter reconciliation sync. Goal today: quick status on Sample A and Sample B, defects we’ve found, what’s landed versus what’s pending, and then timeline for publishing the guidance and enablement.

[00:18] Talia Benson: Laura, anything you want to set at the top?

[00:21] Laura Bennett: Yeah. Just… I’m trying to make sure we don’t get surprised at month-end. If we’re changing anything that touches invoices, I want it clearly scoped, clearly signed off, and we’re not discovering it on the 28th.

[00:35] Talia Benson: Great. Emily, can you do the quick status on reconciliation?

[00:39] Emily Stone: Yep. So Sample A—January—coverage was mostly non-streaming text gen and embeddings. We had 62 accounts in the sample. The median delta between raw telemetry aggregate and billing-ready aggregate was within 0.6%.

[00:56] Emily Stone: But the distribution has a long tail. There were four accounts above 3% delta, and one at 6.1%. That’s the one we asked in Slack if we should hold invoicing, but we didn’t because it was under the materiality threshold for that account.

[01:11] Laura Bennett: And that 6% was… which direction?

[01:14] Emily Stone: Invoice higher than console, and invoice higher than our raw telemetry rollup in a few windows. It looked like duplicates on retry paths.

[01:23] Logan Wright: Yeah, it’s the retry double-counting issue for one endpoint. The event emitter was logging both the initial attempt and the retry as billable. Not always, but enough to show.

[01:32] Nadia Rahman: To be precise, the pipeline couldn’t differentiate outcomes because we weren’t passing request_outcome consistently. So downstream we were just summing tokens by request_id-ish fields that aren’t stable across retries.

[01:45] Talia Benson: Okay. We’ll come back to that. Sample B?

[01:49] Emily Stone: Sample B is February and includes streaming routes. It’s smaller so far—only 28 accounts processed—but it’s designed to over-index on streaming-heavy customers and on the new rerank endpoint.

[02:03] Emily Stone: Early results: we see variance clustering around streaming disconnects, which we expected given ENG-4822 and the PR in flight.

[02:12] Laura Bennett: That’s the thing we might have to backfill, right?

[02:15] Nadia Rahman: Potentially, yeah. There’s a bug where we were continuing to count output tokens after the client disconnect, because the generation loop is still emitting tokens until the cancel propagates.

[02:26] Allison Grant: And the observability side shows spikes in “tokens_out” continuing for a few seconds after disconnect. It’s not like minutes, but it can be non-trivial for long generations.

[02:37] Chloe Martin: That’s also why console was confusing: console uses the usage aggregation table, invoices use the invoice aggregation table, and they weren’t aligned in how they treated the “stream ended early” cases.

[02:49] Talia Benson: Okay. Let’s structure this. Logan/Nadia, can you summarize the defect list and where we are on fixes?

[02:56] Logan Wright: Sure. I’d bucket it as:

[03:00] Logan Wright: One: rounding policy mismatch. Some components were doing per-request rounding to, like, 1K tokens or per-request decimals—depending on meter. Then invoice aggregator is supposed to do aggregate rounding, per ADR. We have a fix PR that removes per-request rounding. That should reduce small systematic deltas.

[03:18] Logan Wright: Two: streaming disconnect accounting. Fix is to stop billing tokens after client disconnect and ensure partial usage is captured correctly. That’s the big one for perception and trust.

[03:30] Logan Wright: Three: retries and request outcomes. Right now, retries can look like extra usage. We need explicit dimensions: retry_reason, request_outcome, and maybe attempt_number. Then billing rules can be “bill only successful tokens” or “bill successful plus partial” depending on policy.

[03:49] Logan Wright: Four: missing dimensions in telemetry events. A few events missing model alias or region; that causes join issues and sometimes gets bucketed into ‘unknown’ which then mismatches invoice line items.

[04:01] Nadia Rahman: And five: time zones / window boundaries. Console shows daily in user TZ; invoices are UTC windows. We have to normalize presentation, but the underlying aggregation windows are UTC.

[04:14] Talia Benson: Great. Laura, I know you’ve asked for clear “what can change invoices.” Let’s talk about impact.

[04:21] Laura Bennett: Yeah. Which of these will cause invoice deltas if we fix it and backfill?

[04:28] Nadia Rahman: Rounding fix should not change materially if we only apply going forward. If we backfill, it will change small amounts across most accounts. That’s why the ADR says do aggregate rounding at invoice time, not per request.

[04:43] Emily Stone: For audit, it’s cleaner to have consistent logic. But Finance would prefer we don’t touch closed periods unless necessary.

[04:50] Rishi Malhotra: Also, if we re-run aggregation logic for January, the “true-up” effect could create noise in revenue reporting, even if small. We need a policy: only backfill when customer-impacting in a meaningful way, or when the defect is clearly overbilling.

[05:06] Laura Bennett: So streaming disconnect is potentially overbilling. That one I’m more open to backfill.

[05:12] Nadia Rahman: Yes, streaming bug is more likely to overbill. Rounding could be either direction depending on distribution.

[05:20] Logan Wright: Retries could be overbilling too, depending on how many retries and how we counted.

[05:25] Sofia Mendes: From legal perspective, the big thing is we need consistency with our “measurement and billing” language. If we say we measure tokens actually generated and delivered, and we’re billing tokens after disconnect, that’s a problem.

[05:39] Laura Bennett: Exactly.

[05:41] Talia Benson: Can we get crisp: are we billing tokens that the customer never received?

[05:45] Nadia Rahman: In some cases, yes. If the client disconnects, they stop receiving, but the backend generation could have emitted further. Those tokens were being counted in the meter.

[05:57] Chloe Martin: Customers compare it to console and they think we’re cooking the books. Even if it’s only, like, a few percent, it’s a trust killer.

[06:06] Talia Benson: Okay. Let’s talk about status of the streaming fix.

[06:10] Nadia Rahman: PR is basically ready. It adds a guard: once disconnect signal is observed, stop incrementing tokens_out. There’s also a fix to ensure partial tokens already sent are still counted. And we have a backfill note: we need to re-run aggregates for the affected window.

[06:27] Allison Grant: We’ll also need alert suppression rules during backfill because the anomaly checks will light up, like “negative deltas” and spikes.

[06:35] Laura Bennett: When can it land?

[06:37] Nadia Rahman: If we get approvals, it can merge today or tomorrow. Rollout next week.

[06:44] Talia Benson: What approvals do you need?

[06:46] Nadia Rahman: Code owner + platform oncall window. And Finance sign-off if we backfill.

[06:52] Laura Bennett: For backfill, I want a one-pager: window, number of impacted accounts, expected revenue impact range.

[06:59] Rishi Malhotra: And it’d help to quantify as gross revenue and net of any credits we might issue, plus a scenario if we choose not to backfill and only correct forward.

[07:09] Logan Wright: We can estimate. The streaming-heavy cohort is not huge, but the top few are big.

[07:15] Talia Benson: Let’s capture that as action item. Nadia/Logan, you’ll send estimate.

[07:20] Nadia Rahman: Yep.

[07:22] Talia Benson: Next: rounding. Chloe, can you talk through console mismatch and status?

[07:28] Chloe Martin: Sure. There was confusion because console usage page rounded at the request level in some components and then summed. Invoice aggregation was summing raw and then rounding. So you’d see console under invoice by, like, 1–2% depending on volume.

[07:45] Chloe Martin: We have changes to normalize time zones and align model alias mapping. But the big behavioral fix is to match the ADR: aggregate then round, not per request. If that lands, console and invoice should be closer.

[07:59] Emily Stone: But we need QA with sample invoices. I want to pick five accounts and compare: invoice PDF line items, billing export, console, and raw telemetry rollups.

[08:10] Talia Benson: Can we do that this coming week?

[08:12] Chloe Martin: Yes, if Finance can join. I’ll set up a session.

[08:16] Laura Bennett: Emily or someone from billing controls should be on it.

[08:19] Emily Stone: Yep.

[08:21] Talia Benson: Next: retries/request outcomes. Logan, what’s the plan there?

[08:27] Logan Wright: The plan is to add request_outcome and retry_reason as dimensions in metering events and downstream aggregation. There’s a PR to add fields, with cardinality safeguards—so we don’t blow up the warehouse.

[08:41] Logan Wright: Then billing rules can exclude certain outcomes. Like, if request failed before first token, do not bill tokens. If partial streaming occurred then disconnect, bill delivered tokens only.

[08:54] Sofia Mendes: We need to be careful about language: do we bill for partial completions if the customer cancels? We should align with terms. Most vendors bill for tokens generated up to cancellation, but “generated” vs “delivered” matters.

[09:09] Laura Bennett: I’d rather we bill delivered. It’s simpler to defend.

[09:12] Nadia Rahman: Technically we can do delivered tokens for streaming because we know what we flushed. For non-streaming, delivered is basically generated if the response completes.

[09:22] Chris Osei: From Product, the thing is: experiment analysis needs stable meters. If we change semantics mid-experiment, we need to annotate and potentially re-run analysis.

[09:32] Talia Benson: Good call. Chris, can you capture that—adding caveats to experiment readouts.

[09:36] Chris Osei: Yeah, I’ll update the registry.

[09:40] Rishi Malhotra: Also, for unit economics we should make sure we’re not accidentally excluding tokens that cost us compute but weren’t delivered, like if the customer cancels after 90% of generation. It’s fair, but margin assumptions shift.

[09:54] Laura Bennett: Sure. But that’s a pricing question; metering has to be defensible.

[09:59] Rishi Malhotra: Agreed.

[10:01] Talia Benson: Okay. Let’s talk acceptance thresholds. Emily, you had suggested a tolerance?

[10:07] Emily Stone: For sanity checks, we initially said absolute delta under 1% at account-month level, and under 2% for streaming-heavy accounts because it’s noisier. But we should tighten once fixes land.

[10:21] Laura Bennett: For close controls, what’s the threshold that triggers a hold or an escalation?

[10:26] Emily Stone: I’d propose: if an account’s invoice differs from billing-ready aggregate by more than 1% AND more than $2k, it triggers investigation before sending invoice. Otherwise, we document and proceed.

[10:41] Laura Bennett: That’s reasonable.

[10:43] Rishi Malhotra: Add also a gross vs net check. A 1% delta on a big account is meaningful even if credits apply later.

[10:50] Emily Stone: Yep.

[10:51] Talia Benson: Allison, from alerts perspective, can we do those checks daily so we’re not discovering at invoice run?

[10:58] Allison Grant: Yes. The design notes include daily reconciliation job comparing raw telemetry aggregates to billing aggregates with per-dimension diffs—model, region, endpoint type. And alert if deltas exceed threshold.

[11:14] Allison Grant: We just need to handle backfills: suppress alerts when invoice_run_id indicates backfill, or add “maintenance windows.”

[11:22] Logan Wright: We can include aggregation_window and invoice_run_id in export schema; it helps audit.

[11:28] Laura Bennett: That’s excellent. Audit wants that.

[11:32] Talia Benson: Switching gears: timeline for publication of guidance. Chris, where are we?

[11:39] Chris Osei: We’re planning to publish three things:

[11:42] Chris Osei: One, canonical meter definitions v3 in Confluence. That includes input/output tokens, cached tokens, embeddings, rerank units, requests, streaming.

[11:52] Chris Osei: Two, invoice line item mapping to telemetry—so Finance and Support can trace line items.

[11:58] Chris Osei: Three, pricing/metering FAQ for AEs and CSMs with talk tracks and the escalation path.

[12:07] Chris Osei: Drafts are about 80%. But we need to incorporate final decisions from the ADR on rounding and streaming accounting.

[12:16] Chloe Martin: The rounding ADR is basically decided: no per-request rounding.

[12:19] Logan Wright: Yeah.

[12:20] Talia Benson: Sofia, legal review timeline?

[12:25] Sofia Mendes: I can turn around the “measurement and billing” guidance quickly, but I need stable product definitions to reference. If we change from “generated” to “delivered” tokens, that’s a substantive update.

[12:39] Laura Bennett: Let’s not re-litigate semantics today. But we should decide within a week.

[12:45] Nadia Rahman: For streaming, we can treat delivered as the source-of-truth. For non-streaming, it’s effectively the same.

[12:52] Sofia Mendes: Okay. I’ll draft language that says “measured based on tokens successfully returned as part of responses,” with carve-outs for retries and system errors.

[13:05] Talia Benson: Great.

[13:06] Talia Benson: I want to check: are we planning to publish guidance before or after the fixes are fully rolled out?

[13:13] Chris Osei: Ideally after, but enablement is needed now because Sales is already getting questions—especially with experiments.

[13:21] Laura Bennett: Publish with a “known issues” section if needed. Just don’t promise something untrue.

[13:27] Chris Osei: Yep.

[13:29] Talia Benson: Let’s do a “current state” plus “changes in flight” section, with expected dates.

[13:35] Emily Stone: And add the dispute runbook link. Support needs it.

[13:39] Talia Benson: Yup.

[13:40] Laura Bennett: Speaking of disputes—any active ones right now that might be impacted?

[13:45] Emily Stone: There’s at least one streaming disconnect complaint. Support ticket references show customer perceives overbilling. It maps pretty cleanly to this bug.

[13:56] Logan Wright: Once we land fix and backfill, we might owe a credit.

[14:02] Laura Bennett: If it’s confirmed, we’ll do it. But I want quantified exposure.

[14:06] Talia Benson: Noted.

[14:08] Rishi Malhotra: For the exec readout, do we have a number? Like $ at risk?

[14:12] Emily Stone: Not yet. We have case log totals but it mixes misunderstanding vs actual defect.

[14:19] Rishi Malhotra: Okay.

[14:21] Talia Benson: Quick aside: experiments. Chris, what do you need from telemetry side to ensure measurements are consistent?

[14:29] Chris Osei: Mainly, we need a meter_version. If the meter definition changes, experiments should log meter_version so analysis can segment or adjust.

[14:41] Logan Wright: We can add meter_version to billing export schema and potentially to the usage dataset. It’s in a PR.

[14:49] Chloe Martin: Console should display meter_version? Maybe too much for customers.

[14:54] Chris Osei: For internal, yes. For external, no.

[14:57] Laura Bennett: Keep customers away from internal complexity. But we need auditability.

[15:03] Talia Benson: Okay.

[15:04] (crosstalk)

[15:05] Nadia Rahman: One point on retries—if we add these dimensions, historical data will not have them. So reconciliation for older periods will still be limited.

[15:13] Emily Stone: That’s fine; for older periods we can accept higher tolerance and document.

[15:18] Sofia Mendes: But the contract language should not rely on fields we didn’t have. It needs to be future-looking and still defensible for past.

[15:27] Talia Benson: Got it.

[15:29] Laura Bennett: Competitor question: Customers keep asking “how do you count tokens compared to OpenAI or Anthropic?” Can we just say we follow standard tokenization and count prompt + completion?

[15:43] Logan Wright: We can say we count input and output tokens using the model’s tokenizer, plus explain streaming.

[15:49] Chris Osei: Sales wants a crisp line: “We bill on tokens processed,” but with the streaming caveat.

[15:56] Sofia Mendes: I’d avoid comparing too directly. Say “we provide transparent usage breakdown in console and invoice mapping.”

[16:04] Laura Bennett: Fair.

[16:06] Talia Benson: Alright. Let’s land on publish timeline.

[16:10] Chris Osei: Proposed:
- Draft meter definitions + mapping by end of this week.
- Final next week after the streaming fix merge.
- Enablement session for AEs/CS the following week.

[16:24] Chloe Martin: Console alignment changes might be next week too.

[16:28] Emily Stone: For close, we need the month-end checklist update before the invoice run.

[16:35] Talia Benson: When’s the invoice run date?

[16:37] Emily Stone: Typically 3rd business day of the month. So early March.

[16:44] Talia Benson: So we have ~2 weeks.

[16:46] Laura Bennett: Make sure the close checklist includes “meter health check, anomaly review, reconciliation sign-off.” And it’s owned.

[16:55] Emily Stone: Yes, I’m owner for that.

[16:58] Allison Grant: We’ll have at least a basic dashboard by then. Full anomaly detection might be iterative.

[17:05] Talia Benson: That’s fine as long as minimum viable controls are in place.

[17:10] Laura Bennett: Exactly.

[17:12] Talia Benson: Any risks to timeline?

[17:15] Nadia Rahman: Biggest risk is backfill safety. We need to ensure invoice_run_id ownership and sequencing so we don’t overwrite production aggregates accidentally.

[17:26] Logan Wright: Also data volume. If we backfill a whole month it’s heavy. We should do a targeted window.

[17:33] Emily Stone: Targeted window is fine. Identify the earliest date the bug was introduced.

[17:38] Nadia Rahman: I think it started around Jan 22 with a streaming service change. Need to confirm.

[17:45] Allison Grant: We can correlate by deploy.

[17:47] Talia Benson: Great.

[17:49] Sofia Mendes: One more: dispute window. We’ve been using 30 days in most contracts, but some prospects ask for 60 or 90. I’ll include recommendation and rationale.

[18:01] Laura Bennett: Good.

[18:03] Talia Benson: Quick check: any open questions we need to answer before next sync?

[18:09] Rishi Malhotra: I want to know how much margin is impacted if we move to delivered tokens. It’s probably small, but quantify.

[18:17] Logan Wright: We can estimate compute wasted on canceled generations.

[18:22] Nadia Rahman: It’s not wasted, it’s just not billed, but yeah.

[18:25] Rishi Malhotra: Right.

[18:26] Chloe Martin: From console side, I need final decisions on how to display cached tokens. Customers see “input tokens” but caching reduces billable? Or reduces cost? Confusing.

[18:39] Chris Osei: Meter definitions doc should say: cached tokens may be billed differently depending on plan. But for now, they’re included in input tokens, right?

[18:47] Nadia Rahman: In Hosted API, cached tokens are tagged but still counted in usage; pricing may discount them in some experiments. That’s why we need meter + price separation.

[19:00] Laura Bennett: Put that clearly in docs. We do not want surprise “you billed me for cached tokens.”

[19:06] Talia Benson: Noted.

[19:07] Talia Benson: Okay, let’s do recap and owners.

[19:10] Talia Benson: Nadia/Logan: streaming disconnect fix landing + backfill estimate and impacted window.

[19:17] Nadia Rahman: Yep.

[19:18] Talia Benson: Emily: top variance accounts list + close checklist update draft.

[19:23] Emily Stone: Yep.

[19:24] Talia Benson: Chloe: schedule QA session console vs invoice.

[19:28] Chloe Martin: Yep.

[19:29] Talia Benson: Sofia: measurement language guidance and dispute window recs.

[19:34] Sofia Mendes: Yep.

[19:35] Talia Benson: Chris: annotate experiment registry with measurement caveats and update publish plan.

[19:41] Chris Osei: Yep.

[19:42] Talia Benson: Allison: alerts—basic daily checks and suppression for backfills.

[19:47] Allison Grant: Yep.

[19:49] Laura Bennett: And I want that one-pager for backfill before anything runs.

[19:54] Nadia Rahman: Understood.

[19:56] Talia Benson: Cool. Thanks everyone. I’ll send notes and action items.

[20:02] (call ends)

---

Notes:
- Several portions had overlapping speech; Fireflies attribution may be imperfect.
- Technical terms like “invoice_run_id” and “meter_version” were mentioned as part of auditability improvements.
- Customer-facing positioning should avoid direct vendor comparisons; focus on transparency and documented measurement.
